{
  "name": "speckit-xref",
  "displayName": "Spec Kit X-Ref",
  "version": "0.12.0",
  "description": "Keeps a GitHub Spec Kit feature and its code tied together inside Claude Code: a new idea researched and shaped with you (or your PRD reviewed and cut into a roadmap), the spec in the system prompt, every edit booked against a task, a proof ladder per requirement, a local dashboard, and an autopilot gated by your decisions and the tests.",
  "author": {
    "name": "Ulrich Diedrichsen",
    "email": "uli@moinsen.dev",
    "url": "https://github.com/moinsen-dev"
  },
  "homepage": "https://github.com/moinsen-dev/speckit-xref",
  "repository": "https://github.com/moinsen-dev/speckit-xref",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": [
    "speckit",
    "spec-kit",
    "spec-driven-development",
    "traceability",
    "drift",
    "mod"
  ],
  "types": "./types/index.d.ts",
  "userConfig": {
    "mode": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Drift mode",
      "description": "advisory: the mod tells the model and the person about drift. strict: it also refuses edits outside the current task's planned or linked files.",
      "default": "advisory",
      "options": [
        "advisory",
        "strict"
      ]
    },
    "driftCheck": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Intent check after each turn",
      "description": "fork: after a turn that changed files, one tool-less question over the session asks whether the change still matches the user's words and the spec. off: deterministic checks only.",
      "default": "fork",
      "options": [
        "fork",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "mapModel": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Model for mapping and transcript-less checks",
      "description": "The model that maps requirements to tasks (/xref map) and runs a drift check when there is no transcript to fork yet (an alias such as haiku, or a model id).",
      "default": "haiku"
    },
    "autopilot": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Autopilot",
      "description": "off: each Spec Kit step waits for you. on: every session starts with the autopilot switched on; after a turn it hands the next step to Claude by itself and stops only for decisions that are yours (/xref auto on|off switches it per session).",
      "default": "off",
      "options": [
        "off",
        "on"
      ]
    },
    "autopilotMaxSteps": {
      "type": "number",
      "title": "Autopilot step budget",
      "description": "How many steps one autopilot run takes before it waits for you.",
      "default": 25
    },
    "review": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Review gates",
      "description": "Where the autopilot stops until you approve (the pane, /xref approve or the dialog). spec+design: at the written spec, and at the design (DESIGN.md and the mocks) of a feature with a user interface. spec: only at the spec. spec+plan / spec+plan+design: also at the plan. none: no review, for maximum autonomy.",
      "default": "spec+design",
      "options": [
        "spec+design",
        "spec",
        "spec+plan",
        "spec+plan+design",
        "none"
      ]
    },
    "testCommand": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Test command",
      "description": "The command that runs the project's tests (e.g. npx vitest run). Empty: derived from plan.md's **Testing**: line. The autopilot runs it after each implement step; failures become repair steps, at most three.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "junitPath": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "JUnit report",
      "description": "Where the test command writes a JUnit XML report (e.g. reports/junit.xml). With it, each requirement is proven by the tests that name or anchor it; without it, a passing suite proves every requirement that has a real test.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "commitPerTask": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Commit per task",
      "description": "on: after an autopilot step whose tests passed, the tasks it checked off are committed with their files (feature branches only, never main; nothing you staged is mixed in; files outside the plan or .env files stop it). off by default.",
      "default": "off",
      "options": [
        "off",
        "on"
      ]
    },
    "parallel": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Parallel [P] tasks",
      "description": "on: a phase's open [P] tasks go to subagents of their own (speckit-xref:task-runner), one per task, and the main agent checks them off. off by default.",
      "default": "off",
      "options": [
        "off",
        "on"
      ]
    },
    "pane": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Open the pane",
      "description": "auto: the pane opens by itself where it is a sidebar (fullscreen). always: it opens with every session in a Spec Kit project (the terminal seats it from 144 columns, 110 once you have opened it; narrower, the band's Pane button opens it). off: only /xref pane opens it.",
      "default": "auto",
      "options": [
        "auto",
        "always",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "validate": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Validate a new idea",
      "description": "on: before a new project's first spec, the idea is researched on the web (who has the problem, what exists, what differs, the riskiest assumption) into .specify/memory/idea-brief.md, and you decide Build, Sharpen or Drop. The idea's wording goes to the web search Claude uses. off: straight to the spec.",
      "default": "on",
      "options": [
        "on",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "shape": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Shape the first version",
      "description": "on: before a new project's first spec, Claude asks you what the idea leaves open (first-version scope, platforms, language, design, data) and records it in .specify/memory/product-brief.md, so the spec treats it as decided. off: the spec decides and calls it assumptions.",
      "default": "on",
      "options": [
        "on",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "design": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Design step",
      "description": "on: a feature with a user interface (plan.md's Project Type) gets its look after the plan and before the tasks: DESIGN.md at the root (Google Stitch's format) and a static HTML mock per screen in specs/<feature>/design/, shown on the dashboard. off: the tasks follow the plan directly.",
      "default": "on",
      "options": [
        "on",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "allowPush": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Push from the autopilot",
      "description": "off: pushing is the person's call; the autopilot asks, and your yes in that dialog allows the one push. on: the autopilot may push a feature branch by itself once the tests are green (never main, master or trunk, never --force, never a deletion).",
      "default": "off",
      "options": [
        "off",
        "on"
      ]
    },
    "acceptance": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Acceptance",
      "description": "auto: after verify, a feature with a user interface is also played through by a scripted driver, scenario by scenario: Playwright for the web (the installed Chrome), Maestro for iOS and Android where it is installed; only the driver's fresh JUnit report accepts a scenario. off (default since 0.8.0): the user test is the check; scripted acceptance runs only when asked.",
      "default": "off",
      "options": [
        "auto",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "orchestrate": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Orchestrate",
      "description": "on (default): implement, repair and the user test run in subagents with a fresh context and a model per step, so the session's context stays small; the session only relays and keeps the spec, the decisions and the reports. off: every step in the session itself.",
      "default": "on",
      "options": [
        "on",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "models": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Models",
      "description": "auto (default): Sonnet implements, repairs and tests, Opus takes over a repair that failed once already and leads a design pass (direction and reviews), Haiku does phases of docs and configuration only; the spec, the reviews, verify and ship stay with the session's own model. sonnet, opus or haiku: that model for every delegated step.",
      "default": "auto",
      "options": [
        "auto",
        "sonnet",
        "opus",
        "haiku"
      ]
    },
    "userTest": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "User test",
      "description": "on (default): a feature with a user interface is used as a person would, in the iOS Simulator of the desktop app or a browser: each story right after it is built, and the whole app before it counts as done; findings become fix tasks, with screenshots. off: no user test.",
      "default": "on",
      "options": [
        "on",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "deputy": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Deputy",
      "description": "full (default): while the autopilot runs, a deputy on Opus reads each step that builds, repairs, tries or restyles the app the way the person would (report, diff, tests) and sends it on, back with a list, or to the person; it answers Claude's questions from the spec, the briefs and the person's own words, and shows what it decided. It never approves a gate, and what only the person decides still goes to them. review: only the reviews. off: neither.",
      "default": "full",
      "options": [
        "full",
        "review",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "tests": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Tests",
      "description": "off (default): no test suite. No test tasks, no tests written, no test gate; the type check of the project's language is the gate (its own typecheck script, tsc, flutter or dart analyze, cargo check, go vet, swift build, mypy, or option checkCommand), and the user test and the deputy check the work. Right for a proof of concept, an MVP or an idea to try. run: no new tests, the existing suite is the gate. lean: one test per requirement or acceptance scenario, the suite is the gate.",
      "default": "off",
      "options": [
        "off",
        "run",
        "lean"
      ]
    },
    "checkCommand": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Check command",
      "description": "The type check that gates each step when tests is off (e.g. `npm run typecheck`). Empty: the mod names the language's usual one.",
      "default": ""
    },
    "ci": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "CI/CD",
      "description": "off (default): the autopilot plans and writes no CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, CircleCI, EAS workflows, fastlane …); writing one in its steps is refused. Asked for in your own words, it is yours. on: allowed.",
      "default": "off",
      "options": [
        "off",
        "on"
      ]
    },
    "git": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Git",
      "description": "current (default): every feature is built on the branch you are on; the autopilot creates or switches no branch. branch: a feature gets its own branch (its folder's name) once its spec is written, from the branch you were on. pr: like branch, and a done feature is committed, pushed and opened as a pull request against that branch; merging stays yours.",
      "default": "current",
      "options": [
        "current",
        "branch",
        "pr"
      ]
    }
  }
}
